title: Brush Up: The 5-Minute Daily News - AI/Tech, Biz, World
description: Your definitive morning intelligence download. Every day shortly after 7:00 AM EST, we bypass the noise to deliver the critical shifts in AI, Global Business, and Macroeconomics that define the modern landscape. Brush up on the news while you brush up your smile.
latestSummary:
India’s revised startup regulations, focused on deep tech like AI and quantum computing, signal a national ambition to lead in technological innovation. Simultaneously, New York lawmakers are considering a three-year moratorium on new data center construction due to environmental concerns surrounding AI’s energy consumption. Benchmark Capital’s $225 million investment in Cerebras highlights continued investor confidence in AI chip competition.

In business news, Coterra Energy and Devon Energy’s $58 billion merger reshapes the energy sector, while Super Micro Computer (SMCI) and Corning (GLW) experienced significant stock jumps driven by strong demand for AI-related hardware and impressive earnings. Congressman Khanna’s investigation into a UAE investment in World Liberty Financial raises concerns about cryptocurrency regulation. General Motors’ dividend increase reflects confidence in its electric vehicle strategy, and falling mortgage rates could stimulate the housing market.

Globally, Japan’s governing party secured a decisive election victory, promising stability. Thailand’s election remains contested, and an investigation is underway regarding the shooting of a Russian general. Protests in Milan, Italy, reflect social tensions ahead of the Olympic Games, and the Washington Post announced a leadership change amid ongoing media industry challenges.

title: Overnight Market Brief - Bridging the Global Gap. Daily.
description:
While North America sleeps, the global economy keeps moving. Overnight Market Brief is your essential pre-market digest, designed for traders, serious investors, and professionals who need to hit the ground running.
Most North American investors miss 50% of the market story because it happens in Tokyo, Hong Kong, and London. We bridge that gap. Every morning at 8:00 AM ET, we deliver a concise, data-driven breakdown and full global picture in under 10 minutes, just in time for your morning commute.
latestSummary:
Wall Street closed defensively on Thursday, with the S&P 500 down 1.2% and the Nasdaq 100 declining 1.4%, driven by risk-off sentiment. The 10-Year Treasury Yield rose to 4.196%, while the US Dollar Index eased slightly to 97.69, and Crude Oil decreased to 63.01. Overnight, Asian markets presented a mixed picture: Tokyo’s Nikkei 225 gained 0.81%, contrasting with declines in Hong Kong (Hang Seng -1.21%) and Shanghai (Composite -0.25%). European markets adopted a cautious approach, influenced by weaker-than-expected German industrial output and contraction in Eurozone construction.

US pre-market futures are higher, with S&P 500 futures up 0.48% and Nasdaq 100 futures up 0.59%, reflecting a rotation into growth stocks. Key catalysts for today’s session include the continued impact of German industrial output data, Swedish inflation data at 2.0%, and ongoing currency dynamics, particularly the dollar’s strength and the Bank of England’s dovish policy. The market currently appears to favor a cautiously higher path, contingent on data releases.

title: Post-market Recap
description:
Did the market "rally into the close" or "fade the open"? The Post-Market Recap goes beyond the green and red arrows to analyze the structure of the trading day. This daily briefing dissects the inter-market correlations that drove the session.
Every afternoon, we cover:
Macro Causality: Connecting the dots between the 10-Year Yield, the Dollar Index, and Equities.
Tech & AI Pulse: A dedicated segment on the semiconductor ecosystem and Big Tech performance.
Market Breadth: Analyzing Volatility (VIX) and Sector Rotation to gauge genuine institutional sentiment.
Closing Catalysts: Identifying the specific news and data that triggered late-day reversals.
latestSummary:
The Post-Market Recap by AGI Era on February 5, 2026, reported a negative day for US markets. The S&P 500 fell 1.23%, closing at 6798.4, while the Nasdaq 100 dropped 1.38% to 24548.69 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average declined 592.58 points to 48908.72. Trading volume was lighter than average, suggesting a lack of strong conviction.

A notable sector rotation occurred, with investors moving into defensive Utilities (XLU.US) which gained 0.09%, while Technology (XLK.US) fell 1.82%, indicating a shift towards safety amid weaker-than-expected labor market readings. The 10-Year Treasury Yield eased to 4.26%, reflecting tempered inflation expectations. The US Dollar Index rose 0.35% to 97.83, and Crude Oil (CL.F) decreased 3.16% to $63.08.

Tech giants experienced significant declines, with Microsoft down 4.97%, Amazon down 4.42%, and Nvidia down 1.27%. This downturn highlighted a broader re-evaluation of growth stocks due to concerns about the economic slowdown. The VIX, the “Fear Gauge,” remained subdued despite the sell-off. Applied Materials (AMAT) saw a notable increase in after-hours trading.

Looking ahead, the market awaits no major economic data releases but will closely monitor Federal Reserve commentary and further labor market updates. The overall tone remains cautious, with investors seeking signs of stabilization or deterioration in economic indicators.

title: Geopolitical Updates
description: Beyond the headlines lies strategy. Geopolitical Updates is your daily guide to the evolving global order. Each episode provides a rapid scan of the day's top international stories, followed by a deep-dive analysis of the single most impactful event shifting the geopolitical landscape. From tension in the South China Sea to economic statecraft in Europe, we explain not just what happened today, but why it matters for tomorrow. Delivered daily at 7 PM ET.
latestSummary:
The Russia-Ukraine conflict is nearing a critical juncture with the United States pushing for a ceasefire by June. Ukrainian President Zelensky acknowledged “difficult issues” remain, as Russia continues targeting Ukrainian energy infrastructure. Simultaneously, Japan held a snap election with Prime Minister Takaichi’s popularity a key factor, potentially reshaping East Asian geopolitics.

In South Asia, authorities arrested four individuals, including a suspected mastermind, in connection with a mosque bombing, raising security concerns. A South Korean cryptocurrency firm accidentally paid out $40 billion in Bitcoin, highlighting risks in the decentralized finance sector. The humanitarian situation in Gaza remains dire, with Palestinians facing stringent inspections at the Rafah crossing.

Finally, former U.S. President Trump threatened tariffs on Iran if trade continues, escalating tensions in the Middle East. These developments collectively underscore shifting global power dynamics, financial vulnerabilities, and ongoing security threats, demanding careful observation across multiple regions.
